summary.text: Andrew Partridge is One Nation's candidate for Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election. Raised on a family farm in western Victoria, he now works in sheep and wool, the ABC says. His past work includes shearing, exporting and managing businesses owned by his family.

sources.title: Lowan: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Emma Kealy has held Lowan for the Nationals since 2014. She has been deputy leader of the Victorian Nationals since July 2022 and is the shadow minister for agriculture and for mental health. Before Parliament she ran the Edenhope and District Memorial Hospital as chief executive. She is recontesting Lowan in 2026.

occupation.text: Health service executive (chief executive of Edenhope and District Memorial Hospital)

prior_roles.role: Deputy Leader of the Victorian Nationals
Shadow Minister for Prevention of Family Violence

prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography gives no years.

legal_and_integrity.text: Referred to the Victorian Ombudsman over newspaper advertising paid from her parliamentary allowance during the election caretaker period.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Responsibility was placed with a newspaper staff member; no action was taken against her.

summary.text: Jeff Moran is standing for the Greens in Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a civil engineer with a background in building roads; his party page says his first job outside Melbourne was at the Country Roads Board in Horsham, where he married and still has family. In 2016 he contested Corio, a federal seat, for Bullet Train for Australia.

previous_candidacies.note: Stood for Bullet Train for Australia.

priorities.text: Repairing and maintaining potholed, unsafe country roads
A sustainable future for younger generations
A progressive voice in Parliament for western Victoria
Putting people ahead of corporate profits

summary.text: Jos Downey is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in rural western Victoria, where he still has family, and describes himself as a socialist activist, organised in the movement from the start of the 2020s. While at university he was active in Students for Palestine and campaigned against the far right and the mandatory detention of refugees.

priorities.text: Workers and ordinary people in Victoria deserve better
A universal living guarantee making essentials affordable and accountable
Expanding emergency services and moving faster to renewable energy
Running aged care, child care and public transport for need rather than private profit
Housing, health care, education and food treated as human rights

sources.title: Lowan: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jos Downey, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Karen Hyslop, a Northern Grampians Shire councillor who was the shire's mayor from 2024 to 2026, is the Australian Democrats candidate for Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election. She won a seat on the council in 2012, came back at a 2022 by-election and has represented Central Ward since 2024, when she polled the most first preferences in the ward. Before entering local government she was a nurse and midwife, and she has lived in Stawell all her life; she joined the Democrats after the party registered in Victoria in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Member, Local Government Mayoral Advisory Panel

previous_candidacies.note: The council gives the year she was first elected but not her ward or the label she stood under.

priorities.text: Repairing country roads
Better health services in rural areas
Easing the cost of living
Keeping the best farming land for agriculture

summary.text: Lee-Ann Elmes is the Family First candidate for Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election; the ABC spells her name this way, while the party's candidate page gives it as Lee Ann Elms. She has a background in education and is president of Hamilton Youth Victoria, a group working to open a youth resource centre in Hamilton. In 2025 she contested Wannon, a federal seat, for Family First.

priorities.text: Communities where young people feel safe, valued and supported
Opening the Stable Ground Hamilton Youth Resource Centre for young people and families
Support for children, young people and families

summary.text: Sue Pavlovich is Labor's candidate for Lowan at the 2026 Victorian election. She lives in Murtoa and has taught students in Horsham for over a decade, and her parents were Polish migrants who arrived after the Second World War. A Sue Pavlovich was fourth on Labor's Western Victoria upper-house ticket in 2022, though no source confirms this is the same person (unverified).

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Sue Pavlovich fourth on Labor's Western Victoria ticket; only the name matches, and no source links her to this candidate. Labor won two seats from its ticket.

priorities.text: Treating education as the most important investment in children's futures
Women's health, including Labor's health services for women in the Wimmera
Being a strong local voice for the people of Lowan
